I’m 53 years old and I’ve been farming these 12 mu in Quzhou County since I was a young man. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer labels and I usually listen to what the extension agent says, though I don’t always follow it exactly — I’d rather be a little safe than sorry. I don’t have a big business farm; this is family land, and every yuan I spend on inputs has to come back.

This year I’m sticking with what I know works. I’ll plant winter wheat on 10 mu in mid-October. Wheat is the backbone of our food security — we eat the flour all year, and the straw feeds our animals. I’ll use an improved variety like *jimai22*, the same kind my neighbor Lao Wang used last year with good results. For soil prep I’ll do rotary tillage to break up the maize stubble and get a fine seedbed. The extension agent recommends about 12–13 kg of nitrogen per mu, but two years ago I cut back to 12 and the tillers were weak, so I went back to 15 kg N per mu and the crop looked much greener. I’ll put down compound fertilizer as base dressing — about 15 kg N, 5 kg phosphorus, and 2 kg potassium per mu — and topdress with urea at jointing. Water is costly but a dry spring would ruin me, so I’ll irrigate four times: once before winter, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. For pests I’ll spray herbicide once after emergence, insecticide twice for aphids, and fungicide once if the weather turns damp — about four sprays in total. If the spring isn’t too dry I expect around 480 kg per mu.

Right after wheat harvest in early June I’ll plant summer maize on the same 10 mu. The window is tight — less than a week — so there’s no time for tillage. I’ll plant no-till directly into the wheat stubble using a hybrid variety like *denghai605*. Maize needs good nitrogen, so I’ll apply about 14 kg N per mu; I won’t add extra phosphorus or potassium because the wheat fertilizer left enough in the soil. I’ll irrigate twice, around silking and grain filling, and spray three times for weeds and corn borers. I’m hoping for about 520 kg per mu.

The remaining 2 mu I’ll plant cotton in the spring. Cotton is more work and needs a lot of pesticide, but the price has been decent and my wife can help with the picking. I’ll rotary till in April and use an improved variety. I’ll apply about 10 kg N, 3 kg phosphorus, and 2 kg potassium per mu, irrigate twice, and spray about 10 times through the season for bollworms and aphids. I expect around 220 kg per mu.

This plan keeps my family fed, provides some cash income, and doesn’t take risks I’m not comfortable with at my age.
